standards.name: MI2CAST (Minimum Information about a Molecular Interaction Causal Statement)
standards.abstract: MI2CAST defines the minimum metadata needed to represent directed causal relationships between biological entities (source → target), where the research objects are molecular causal statements (genes, RNAs, proteins, chemicals, complexes, cells, or processes) observed under experimental or literature-derived conditions. The guidelines specify which identifiers, controlled-vocabulary terms and contextual annotations should accompany a causal assertion (e.g., causal relationship, evidence, experimental setup, biological activity, taxon and cellular context). MI2CAST is a community-maintained effort (documentation and examples hosted on GitHub) and was published in Bioinformatics (2020); it addresses homogenizing curation and annotation of causal molecular interactions to improve FAIRness and interoperability by recommending ontologies and concrete fields to include with each curated causal statement.

classification.rationale: The source contains explicit tabular summaries that name individual terms/fields (e.g., “source entity”, “causal relationship”, “reference(s)”) along with short definitions, recommended ontologies/controlled vocabularies and mandatory/optional flags. This is genuine field-level structure (rows/columns) and therefore should be extracted as a Metadata Table.

source_entity.name: source entity
source_entity.descr: Regulator entity — the biological entity acting as the source/regulator in a causal statement; a unique identifier must be provided.
source_entity.evidence: "A unique identifier must be provided to identify the specific biological entity involved in the causal statement."

raw_full_info.recommended_ontologies: ensembl gene ID, Entrez gene ID, RNAcentral, Ensembl transcript ID, UniProt ID, ChEBI, ComplexPortal (for stable complexes) or lists of component IDs for families/transient complexes

target_entity.name: target entity
target_entity.descr: Regulated entity — the biological entity acted upon by the source; a unique identifier must be provided.
target_entity.evidence: "A causal statement has at least one source entity and one target entity."

raw_full_info.recommended_ontologies: Entrez gene ID, UniProt ID, GO (for phenotypes), Cell Ontology for cells

causal_relationship.name: causal relationship
causal_relationship.descr: Regulatory outcome exerted by source on target (e.g., up-regulates, down-regulates).
causal_relationship.evidence: "The causal relationship corresponds to the regulatory outcome exerted by the source entity upon the target entity."

reference.name: reference(s)
reference.descr: Publication(s) or primary report(s) where the causal interaction was curated from; provenance for the statement.
reference.evidence: "The provenance of the causal statement corresponds to the reference to scientific reports and provides data consumers information about the quality of an annotation: In which publication this causal relationship has been found?"

evidence_type.name: type of evidence
evidence_type.descr: Assessment of how the causal interaction was supported (experimental procedure, curation, computational inference, etc.).
evidence_type.evidence: "The evidence type corresponds to experiment or any data the causal interaction is based: How was the causal interaction proven and generated?"

experimental_setup.name: experimental setup(s)
experimental_setup.descr: Particular experimental conditions/designs applied to the entities that support the causal interaction (e.g., overexpression, engineered constructs); optional, when known.
experimental_setup.evidence: "If the type of evidence is an experiment, the experimental setup corresponds to a particular experimental conditions supporting the experiment. It specifies the design of the two entities (e.g., overexpression of the source entity)."

biological_activity.name: biological activity
biological_activity.descr: Molecular function(s) of the entities involved in the causal interaction (e.g., kinase activity, binding activity); annotate if known.
biological_activity.evidence: "The biological activity corresponds to the molecular activity of the entity causing the regulation or that is regulated (e.g., kinase activity, binding activity)."

biological_mechanism.name: biological mechanism
biological_mechanism.descr: Biological process or mechanism describing the causal effect (used if biological activity is unknown).
biological_mechanism.evidence: "If this information is not available, the biological mechanism of the causal statement that constitutes the biological effect of the source entity on the target entity ... should be provided, if available."

raw_full_info.recommended_ontologies: PSI-MI terms for causal interaction or interaction type branch

biological_type.name: biological type
biological_type.descr: Biological nature/type of the entity (interactor type) — annotate when ambiguous or when identifier does not convey correct type.
biological_type.evidence: "biological type | biological nature of the entity ... | if ambiguous or incorrect from the entity's identifier"

taxon.name: taxon
taxon.descr: Taxonomic identifier for the organism where the causal interaction is observed or to which the entity belongs; include if it cannot be inferred from identifiers.
taxon.evidence: "taxon | the taxon where the causal interaction is observed or where the entity is from | NCBI Taxonomy | if can't be inferred"

biological_modification.name: biological modification(s)
biological_modification.descr: State(s), physical configuration(s) or conformations of an entity (post-translational modifications, isoforms, processed forms) — annotate if present.
biological_modification.evidence: "biological modification(s) | physical configuration(s) or conformation(s) of an entity | [see doc] | if any"

raw_full_info.recommended_ontologies: (see guideline section on biological modification for recommended terms/ontologies)

compartment.name: compartment
compartment.descr: Cellular location where the causal interaction is observed or where an entity is present (e.g., nucleus, cytoplasm).
compartment.evidence: "compartment | cellular location the causal interaction is observed in or the entity is present | GO:CC | if known"

tissue_type.name: tissue type
tissue_type.descr: Tissue in which the causal interaction is observed (when applicable).
tissue_type.evidence: "tissue type | the tissue structure with a specific function in which the causal interaction is observed | BRENDA, Uberon, PO, FAO | if known"

raw_full_info.recommended_ontologies: BRENDA Tissue Ontology, Uberon, Plant Ontology (PO), Fungal Anatomy Ontology (FAO)

cell_line_or_cell_type.name: cell line or cell type
cell_line_or_cell_type.descr: Cell culture or specific cell type where the causal interaction is observed or occurs.
cell_line_or_cell_type.evidence: "cell line or cell type | the cell culture or form where the causal interaction is observed or occurs | CL, BRENDA, Cellosaurus | if known"

raw_full_info.recommended_ontologies: Cell Ontology (CL), BRENDA Tissue/Cell Ontology, Cellosaurus

standards.notes: Fields extracted correspond to terms explicitly presented in MI2CAST summary tables and guideline Rule sections; recommended ontologies/IDs were preserved in raw_full_info where the guideline lists them.
